pr_title: volume: mask password in cifs mount error messages
pr_body:
In managed environment (such as Nomad clusters), users are not always
supposed to see credentials used to mount volumes.
However, if errors occur (most commonly, misspelled mount paths), the
error messages will output the full mount command -- which might contain
a username and a password in the case of CIFS mounts.

This PR detects password=... when error messages are wrapped and masks
them with ********.

Closes https://github.com/fsouza/go-dockerclient/issues/905.
Closes https://github.com/hashicorp/nomad/issues/12296.
Closes https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/43596.

Signed-off-by: Sebastian Höffner <sebastian.hoeffner@mevis.fraunhofer.de>

<!--
Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines;
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

** Make sure all your commits include a signature generated with `git commit -s` **

For additional information on our contributing process, read our contributing
guide https://docs.docker.com/opensource/code/

If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
"closes #xxxx"

Please provide the following information:
-->

**- What I did**
In the error handler for cifs mounts, `password=...` will be masked with `********` in user facing error messages.

**- How I did it**
- Added `func getPassword(opts string) string` in line with `getAddr` (could potentially be refactored into something such as `func getOption(opt string, opts string) string`)
- Added unit tests for getPassword
- Replaced `password=[detectedPassword]` with `password=********`

**- How to verify it**
Was:
```console
$ docker volume create --driver local --opt type=cifs --opt "o=username=shoeffner,password=supersecretpassword,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0777,dir_mode=0777" --opt device=//192.168.1.2/Public cifstest
$ docker run --rm -it -v cifstest:/themnt busybox bash
docker: Error response from daemon: error while mounting volume '/var/lib/docker/volumes/cifstest/_data': failed to mount local volume: mount //192.168.1.2/Public:/var/lib/docker/volumes/cifstest/_data, data: username=shoeffner,password=supersecretpassword,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0777,dir_mode=0777: permission denied.
```
Is:
```console
$ docker volume create --driver local --opt type=cifs --opt "o=username=shoeffner,password=supersecretpassword,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0777,dir_mode=0777" --opt device=//192.168.1.2/Public cifstest
$ docker run --rm -it -v cifstest:/themnt busybox bash
docker: Error response from daemon: error while mounting volume '/var/lib/docker/volumes/cifstest/_data': failed to mount local volume: mount //192.168.1.2/Public:/var/lib/docker/volumes/cifstest/_data, data: username=shoeffner,password=********,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0777,dir_mode=0777: permission denied.
```

**- Description for the changelog**
<!--
Write a short (one line) summary that describes the changes in this
pull request for inclusion in the changelog:
-->
Passwords in user facing error messages for CIFS mounts are masked.

**- A picture of a cute animal (not mandatory but encouraged)**

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1836815/168321285-b249cf28-c2bc-467f-a321-f90cde684fa8.png)
https://www.pexels.com/photo/cold-nature-cute-ice-52509/

I'm also wondering if these options would still be leaking in other ways (e.g., would `mount` show them? `docker volume inspect` ?) -I haven't checked, but mostly thinking out loud. Passing a password as command line arg is, erm, well, never ideal.

So, I'm ok with fixing the error, but it still somewhat tapers over the issue 😅

You are completely right that it will still be possible to use `inspect`, and there are many other ways. But in the particular use case in https://github.com/hashicorp/nomad/issues/12296#issue-1169667160, the user will only see `username=${MOUNT_USERNAME},password=${MOUNT_PASSWORD}` in their configuration; Nomad will fill those environment variables with secrets from Vault. Thus, in normal (successful) operation, a user will never see those parameters. But if they got some options wrong, most often this happens with the path they want to mount, this will be logged very prominently in the Nomad web UI. And of course, requesting support, users will copy, screenshot, etc. those errors without further thinking, accidentally leaking the passwords to various chats, forums, etc...

So while this will not help to stop nefarious actors from stealing credentials, it will make the surface for unintentional copying slightly smaller – in the case of Nomad it should almost vanish.

For me, this was the most obvious solution to fix this, but now that you question this, I checked the docs (https://linux.die.net/man/8/mount.cifs) and it seems to be possible to provide a credentials file: `credentials=...`. Maybe that might actually be a better solution than "hiding" the fact that the password is still readable. Do you happen to know if that works with docker, and if that file should be on the host system or inside the container?

I updated the code to replace the password inside the error message instead of the oroginal mount options. However, if you think the clean solution is to use the credentials file (and it is somehow possible), then it is perfectly fine to not move forward with this PR.

I think another colleague looked into passing the credentials via files at first, but IIUC, credential files are handled by the `mount` tool itself, not actually supported by the kernel. (I don't know, maybe it would give rise to a different set of issues if the syscall handler would have to read files for the credentials. OTOH mounting is not exactly functionality that can entirely ignore filesystems…)

> it seems to be possible to provide a credentials file: credentials=....

>  think another colleague looked into passing the credentials via files at first, but IIUC, credential files are handled by the mount tool itself, not actually supported by the kernel. 

Yes, correct; I think there's some existing discussions around that; the docker daemon uses a plain mount, and won't use the mount tool / helpers. (Also see the discussion in https://github.com/docker/cli/issues/2802, but there may be other tickets discussing that)

> It seems a little bit hacky, but overall sane/simple enough IMO 👍 

This could would only be hit in case of an error, so while (perhaps) optimisations could be made, it won't affect the regular code paths, so I think that's fine.

**Description**

For cifs mounts, sensitive passwords might be leaked in user facing error messages.
This is the case when, e.g., using hashicorp's nomad with secret credentials from vault (For details, please refer to https://github.com/hashicorp/nomad/issues/12296 and https://github.com/fsouza/go-dockerclient/issues/905).
While this is kind of a security issue, it's not really one as the credentials would be accessible via inspect, debug logs, or, if not using docker, in fstab anyways.

<!--
Briefly describe the problem you are having in a few paragraphs.
-->

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Create a cifs volume, the exact parameters do not matter, they should contain a password and be wrong, however:
    ```console
    $ docker volume create --driver local --opt type=cifs --opt "o=username=shoeffner,password=supersecretpassword,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0777,dir_mode=0777" --opt device=//192.168.1.2/Public cifstest
    ```
2. Mount the volume:
    ```console
    $ docker run --rm -it -v cifstest:/themnt busybox bash
    docker: Error response from daemon: error while mounting volume '/var/lib/docker/volumes/cifstest/_data': failed to mount local volume: mount //192.168.1.2/Public:/var/lib/docker/volumes/cifstest/_data, data: username=shoeffner,password=supersecretpassword,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0777,dir_mode=0777: permission denied.
    ```

**Describe the results you received:**
See above, the password is printed.

**Describe the results you expected:**
The password is masked.

review_comments:
The only concern I have with this, is that this can hide the underlying error-type, which would prevent detecting (e.g.) `errors.Is(err, fs.NotExist)`.

It looks like currently we don't do any detection of error-types, and consider any error to be a "500" (internal server error) (probably not correct either for this case 🤔 but that's a separate issue); https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/4cac624fefefb7bb6640f205587d0dc0a9651b27/volume/local/local.go#L315-L317

Let me at least get some eyes from @cpuguy83 on this as well

I was concerned about this implementation, but in `mount.cifs(8)` we have the following delightful gem: :see_no_evil: :heart:

```
              Note  that  a  password  which  contains the delimiter character
              (i.e. a comma ',') will fail to be parsed correctly on the  com‐
              mand  line. However, the same password defined in the PASSWD en‐
              vironment variable or via a credentials file (see below) or  en‐
              tered at the password prompt will be read correctly.
```
